⚠️ THE LARGEST REAL GAP IN THE CORPUS. 29 recipe lines, the single biggest unanswered term, and the library had NO row for sodium bicarbonate under any of its four English names. ⚠️ WHY IT WAS MISSING, AND IT IS NOT AN EXTRACTION PROBLEM. AGROVOC c_26825 is the only source in the library that names it, holding sodium bicarbonate as its English prefLabel with baking soda and bicarbonate of soda as altLabels, in six languages. AGROVOC anchors ZERO of the 41,825 entries it supplies, so a concept only it carries cannot become a row. The term is in join.db, it is in the loaded vocabulary, and it was invisible to every tool: not on the cut sheet, which records removals from rows that existed, not on the scan sheet, which lists holders, and not reachable by extraction, which reads rows.
⚠️ AND OPENING THE ANCHOR WAS MEASURED AND DECLINED. Letting AGROVOC anchor would create 39,473 rows. 30 read at random gave 0 ingredients: species binomials, soil and ocean science, lab technique, farm management, and outright non-topics such as encyclopaedias and halitosis. Worse than a coin flip, so the concept is authored one at a time instead and the seed does the provenance work. See docs/reading-a-holder.md.
